chunks: Al-Sayyari, from the one who reported it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who is keen to reduce his anger, so let him eat the meat of the pheasant'.

key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: The Messenger of Allah (Prophet Muhammad SAWW)

ai.seo_question: How can eating pheasant meat help reduce anger according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* under the chapter on bird meats, this hadith presents a specific dietary remedy for emotional regulation, linking the consumption of pheasant meat to the mitigation of anger. Within Shia scholarly tradition, this reflects the broader concept of *tadabbur al-tibb* (reflection on medicine), where physical sustenance is viewed as a means to stabilize the humors and, by extension, the soul's temperamental disposition.

en.hubeali: Al Sayyari, from the one who reported it,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who is keen to reduce his anger, so let him eat the meat of the pheasant’.
en.sarwar: 3. Al-Sayyariy has narrated from those who narrated to him who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘
If reducing one’s anger makes him happy he should eat partridge meat.’”
